title: Business Intelligence Karachi: Data & Power BI | 22 Signals
description: Business intelligence Karachi manufacturers, distributors and listed firms rely on: one version of sales, margin and stock, in Power BI or Looker Studio.
eyebrow: Business Intelligence and Data Analytics in Karachi
h1: Business intelligence Karachi leadership teams can trust on Monday morning
intro: Our business intelligence and data analytics work gives Karachi companies one reliable view of sales, margin, stock and cash. We connect ERP, accounting, CRM and spreadsheet data into a warehouse, build dashboards in Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau, and automate the reports managers currently build by hand. It suits manufacturers, distributors, exporters, retailers and listed companies.

p: In many Karachi head offices the numbers arrive by email. Each region sends its own Excel file, finance reconciles them with the ERP, and by the time the management pack reaches the directors the month is half over. Two departments quote two different sales figures in the same meeting, and both can explain why theirs is right.

Business intelligence fixes that by agreeing the definitions once, pulling the data automatically and showing everyone the same figures. The aim is not prettier charts. It is faster, calmer decisions based on numbers people stop arguing about.

A typical first brief from a Karachi distributor sounds like this: we have twelve sales officers, three warehouses and a scheme every month, and we cannot tell which scheme worked. Good business intelligence Karachi teams can act on answers that question within days of the month closing, not weeks, and shows the answer down to route and outlet level.

list: Data strategy and KPI design: which measures matter, how each one is calculated and who owns it.
Data warehouse and pipelines that pull from SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Odoo, local accounting software, CRMs and spreadsheets.
Dashboards in Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau, built for the people who will open them every day.
Automated reporting: board packs, weekly sales summaries and exception alerts delivered by email or WhatsApp.
Forecasting for demand, cash flow and stock, with the method explained.
Data quality checks so missing or duplicate records are caught before they reach a report.

sections.h: What Karachi industries want to see
list: FMCG and consumer goods: secondary sales by distributor and route, scheme spend against uplift, and stock days at each warehouse.
Textile and apparel exporters: margin per order after yarn, dyeing and freight costs, plus on-time shipment rates by buyer.
Shipping, freight and logistics: container turnaround, demurrage exposure and revenue per client across Karachi Port and Port Qasim jobs.
Retail chains with branches in Clifton, DHA, Gulshan and beyond: sales per square foot, sell-through and returns by store.
Listed companies on the Pakistan Stock Exchange: board and audit committee reporting that ties back to the ledger.
Banks, insurers and fintechs: product, channel and branch performance, kept separate from customer-level data where policy demands it.

sections.h: How we deliver: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we sit with the people who use the numbers, from the CFO to a regional sales manager, and list the decisions they make each week.
Plan: we audit your data sources, agree KPI definitions in writing and design the dashboards on paper before building anything.
Build: pipelines first, then the model, then the dashboards. We test every figure against your existing reports and explain any difference.
Grow: we train your team, hand over documentation and keep improving the reports as new questions come up.

We have managed over $1.5 million in projects, and every one of them was run against written budgets and dates. We bring the same habit to your data: if a number matters to the business, it should have a clear definition, an owner and a check.

sections.h: Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau?
p: Many Karachi companies already pay for Microsoft 365, which makes Power BI the natural choice: row-level security, Excel familiarity and a good fit with Azure. Businesses that run on Google Workspace or Google Ads often start with Looker Studio. Tableau suits teams with heavy analyst use. We recommend based on your licences, users and data, not on preference, and we can work within an existing setup rather than starting over.

sections.h: Data rules and who can see what
p: Dashboards spread data quickly, so access control is part of the design. Sales managers see their region, directors see the whole company, and customer-level information is limited to the people who need it. For SBP-regulated firms we keep processing locations and access logs documented. We follow PECA 2016 on unauthorised access and plan around the principles in Pakistan's draft Personal Data Protection Bill.
We are not your auditors or legal advisers, but we make it straightforward for them to see where each number comes from.

A Signal Lead runs your project and is your single contact. Reviews are booked at times that suit your finance and sales teams, and each one starts from a written note of what was loaded, checked and changed. Data work is done securely on your systems or ours by agreement, and on-site time is arranged only when the project needs it.

list: Number and type of data sources, and whether they have APIs.
How clean the data is today.
Number of dashboards, users and security roles.
Licensing for Power BI, Tableau or cloud warehouse services.
Whether you want ongoing support and new reports each month.

p: The business intelligence Karachi firms usually buy stops at the dashboard. Ours connects to what happens next: AI forecasting, automation of the reports, cloud hosting for the warehouse and, where it helps, marketing data from Google and Meta in the same view. One team, one lead. Related: Power BI Consulting, Data Engineering, AI Automation and Cloud Consulting.

faqs.q: What is business intelligence for a Karachi company?
faqs.a: It is the system that turns your scattered operational data into reliable reports and dashboards. For a Karachi manufacturer or distributor that usually means sales, stock, margin and cash pulled automatically from the ERP and spreadsheets into one place, so management sees the same figures every morning instead of waiting for month-end files.

faqs.q: Can you work with SAP, Oracle or local accounting software?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with large ERPs and with the smaller accounting packages common in Pakistan, as well as CRMs and Excel files. Where a system has an API we use it; otherwise we use scheduled exports or read-only database access. We confirm the method for each source before the build starts.

faqs.q: Do you build Power BI dashboards in Urdu?
faqs.a: We can label dashboards in Urdu if your users prefer it, though most Karachi management teams work in English for reporting. We also write the KPI definitions and training notes in the language your team is most comfortable with, so the person opening the dashboard understands exactly what each number means.

faqs.q: How long before we see the first dashboard?
faqs.a: It depends on how many sources need connecting and how clean the data is. We usually deliver the first working dashboard on one priority area, often sales, before moving on to the rest, so you see value early. The full timeline is agreed during planning and written into the scope.

faqs.q: Is our financial data safe with you?
faqs.a: We use role-based access, encrypted connections and audit logs, and we only take the access the project needs. Where your policy or the State Bank of Pakistan requires data to stay in specific locations, we design the warehouse accordingly. You keep ownership of all data, pipelines and reports.

faqs.q: Can business intelligence Karachi retailers use include online sales?
faqs.a: Yes. We combine branch POS data with your online store, marketplace and cash-on-delivery records, plus ad spend from Google, Meta and TikTok where useful. That shows true performance by channel and lets you see, for example, which campaigns drive store visits as well as orders.
